newsitem.title: USA: Calif. official sees $450 mln windfall for state.
newsitem.headline: Calif. official sees $450 mln windfall for state.

text.p: California will probably take in an additional $450 million in tax revenues this fiscal year as a result of cuts in the federal capital gains tax rate, the state's director of finance said Monday.

Director of Finance Craig Brown, who spoke with reporters hours after Calif. Gov. Pete Wilson signed the state's $67 billion budget, said the budget does not include an estimated $450 million the state will likely receive as a result of investors cashing in on the federal capital gains tax cuts.
Brown said the figure of $450 million was based on projections made by the state's Franchise Tax Board.
The federal budget package signed earlier this month by President Bill Clinton cut the capital gains tax rate to 20 percent from 28 percent for investments held at least 18 months.
